# Restore rehearsal

<!-- GENERATED by `scripts/restore-rehearsal.sh`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Rehearsed 2026-09-09 10:42 UTC. Dump `lnd-20260909T104217Z.dump`, restored into `lnd_restore`. Backup, restore and verification together: 7 seconds.

## Why this document exists

The plan has recorded restore-from-backup as *configured, not proven* since week 2, and the runbook refused to claim otherwise. `pg_restore` exiting zero proves a file was readable; it does not prove the restored database still enforces what the original enforced. Three things are checked here, and the second is the one that would have been missed.

## What the backup is

One `pg_dump -Fc` per night, taken as the owning role — the application role has no UPDATE on `raw` and no CREATE anywhere, so a dump taken as `lnd_app_rw` would be missing exactly the parts that matter. Streamed to the host rather than written inside the container: a backup on the same volume as the data it protects is not a backup. Pruned at 30 days.

Until week 10 the nightly dump was a comment in `compose.prod.yaml` and nothing took one. WAL archiving was configured and the base backup it recovers *from* was not — recovery that looks provisioned and has no starting point. `scripts/backup.sh` is the missing half.

## 2. Raw is still append-only

Roles live in the cluster, not in the dump. A restore into a fresh cluster can succeed completely and arrive with every grant referring to a role that does not exist — a platform that looks identical and has lost the guarantee it was built on. Asked of the restored database:

## Result

**Passed.** Every grain, every grant and every published figure survived the round trip. Backup, restore and verification together took 7 seconds on the dev stack.

Read that number as a lower bound. It is a local dump over a loopback socket against a dataset of a few thousand rows; production adds a network, a larger volume and whoever has to be woken up. The shape of the operation is what has been proven here, not its duration.

## What is still not proven

**Point-in-time recovery.** WAL archiving is configured in `compose.prod.yaml` and this rehearsal restores a base dump only. Replaying WAL forward to a chosen moment is a different procedure with a different failure mode, and claiming it works because a dump restored would be the same mistake this document was written to end.

**A fresh cluster.** The restore above went into a database on a cluster that already had the roles. `scripts/restore.sh` checks for them and stops with the remedy rather than restoring a database whose access control did not survive, but the disaster case — new host, empty cluster — has not been walked end to end.
